sentences.text: Prayagdutt Shivhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13
September, 2019

Author: Vishal Mishra
Bench: Vishal Mishra
 1 Mcrc-37087-2019
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Mcrc-37087-2019
 (Prayagdutt Shivhare Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
Gwalior, Dated : 13-09-2019
Shri Awdhesh Singh Bhadauria, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Ankit Saxena PP, appearing on behalf of respondent/State.
This is first application u/S. 439 Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

He has been arrested by Police Station since 8.8.2019 STF, Bhopal Unit, Gwalior, in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offences punishable u/S.420, 272, 273, 120B of the IPC and 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standard Adhiniyam, 2006.
I t is submitted by counsel for the applicant that the applicant is a businessman and selling food-grains having license Annexure P/2.
He is doing business in the name of Navin Trading Company.
He has filed a document to the Commercial Tax Department showing his business activities.
It is further submitted that he is only a supplier of the goods and has not committed any offence of adulteration of food articles and he has been falsely implicated in the case.

It is alleged by the counsel for the applicant that FIR has been registered for the aforesaid offences under IPC whereas the case in hand relates to Food Safety and Standards Act and should have been governed by the provisions of Food Safety Act.
The Sections of IPC are wrongly made applicable to the case of the applicant and they are not made out in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It is submitted that offence under section 420 of IPC has been registered against the applicant.

From the bare perusal of reading of Section 420 and 415 of IPC, it is apparently clear that in the facts and circumstances of the present case the aforesaid Sections are not attracted for the reason that there is no person who has made any complaint against the applicant regarding cheating and until and unless the basic requirement of Sections 415 and 420 of IPC are completed, no offence is made out against the applicant under the aforesaid Sections.

He has drawn attention of this Court to 2 MCRC-37087-2019 other Sections 272 and 273 of IPC and has argued that when specific Act is being provided with specific sections which has not been taken into consideration by the authorities and has registered the case under the Indian Penal Code.
The act of the present applicant if taken to be correct then also the provisions of Food Safety Act are applicable in the case and not that of IPC.
Thus, he has argued that Sections 272 and 273 read with Section 120 of IPC are wrongly being made applicable to the case of the applicant.

Thus, even under the Food Safety Act the offence is not made out as the procedure which has been adopted by the authorities of STF is not the proper procedure Prayagdutt Shivhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184390645/
1 and the authorities being incompetent authorities to Act under the Food Safety Act. The aforesaid procedure is to be done by the officer authorized as per act.

sentences.text: He has further argued that even if the offences are taken to be proved against the present applicant except 420 then also there is only an imprisonment of six months.

There is no criminal history against the present applicant, therefore,
prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.

Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application and has submitted that the investigation is pending consideration, therefore till the investigation is completed the applicant is not entitled for grant of bail rather he should be directed to cooperate with the investigation as the offences which have been registered are not the offences against the particular person, the aforesaid offences are offences against the society at large by the act of the present applicant dealing into manufacturing in sale of adulterated food products which are dangerous for human consumption and could have resulted fatal for a person consuming the same.

He has further submitted that several articles have been seized from the custody of the present applicant and his premises,
therefore, until the investigation is completed, he should not be granted bail.

It is further contended that the offences under IPC have rightly been registered against the present applicant as the offences under Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 were also registered along with.

It is further submitted that the 3 MCRC-37087-2019 proceedings are being carried out by the STF which is duly being constituted under the instructions of Superintendent of Police, STF Gwalior comprising of three persons out of which one is from the STF Police Department and two others were from the Food Safety Department.
Thus, the proceedings are being carried out by the authorized persons.
He further submitted that bail application of co-accused has been rejected by this court vide M.Cr.C.No.3585 of 2019 There is active participation of the present applicant in commission of offence.
Therefore, he prayed for rejection of the same.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard and Case-diary is perused.
An STF has been constituted under the instructions of Superintendent of STF Gwalior and comprising of a person from the STF Police Department and the two others from the Food Safety Department.
The inquiry is pending consideration in the matter and the alleged offences which have been committed by the applicant are offences at large against the society.

The applicant is involved in manufacture and sale of adulterated food materials which are dangerous and harmful for human consumption because the same results to various uncurable diseases which ultimately results into deaths.
Thus, in the opinion of this Court until the investigation is completed in the matter no bail should be granted to the applicant.

Accordingly, finding no merits in the application the same is hereby rejected at this stage.
CC as per rules.

(VISHAL MISHRA)
 R. K. SHARMA JUDGE
